mechanism_inventory: external-call failure / DoS on native refund path (unhandled revert in refund.call silently discards funds)
stuck funds / permanent token lock when ERC20 target call fails with no token recovery path
precision / packing / normalization edge — remainingBalance underflow if a fee-on-transfer or rebasing token reduces balanceOf below initBalance
missing invariant enforcement — approve(paymentOperator, amount) is never reset to zero after the call, leaving a residual allowance exploitable by paymentOperator
access-control mismatch — onlyOwner on both overloads means caller-supplied paymentOperator receives the full ERC20 allowance and can drain the approved amount independently
external-call failure / DoS — if token.transferFrom reverts, entire execute reverts with no native refund issued
value exceeds logical bound — extraNative forwarded to target.call; on failure only extraNative is refunded but ERC20 tokens already approved are not recovered

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: When token == address(0) and target.call fails, the fallback refund.call{value: amount}('') result is discarded (`(refund.call{value: amount}(''));`). If refund is a contract that reverts, the native ETH is permanently stuck in UTBExecutor with no further recovery path.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any actor who controls the refund address (a malicious contract that reverts on receive) or any scenario where the refund address becomes non-payable. Owner (UTB) initiates, but the refund recipient is user-supplied and untrusted.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. execute(target, ..., token=address(0), amount=X, refund=MaliciousContract). 2. target.call{value:X}(payload) fails. 3. refund.call{value:X}('') reverts inside MaliciousContract.receive(). 4. Failure silently ignored (discarded tuple). 5. X wei stuck permanently in UTBExecutor.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: End-user / initiator loses native ETH permanently stuck in UTBExecutor.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Nobody — funds locked, not stolen (griefing/DoS on refund path).
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: `(refund.call{value: amount}(''));` discards the bool with no revert/retry. Distinct mechanism affecting native ETH balance and user ETH victim.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In the ERC20 path, IERC20(token).approve(paymentOperator, amount) grants paymentOperator a live allowance; paymentOperator is caller-supplied with no validation. paymentOperator can call token.transferFrom(UTBExecutor, attacker, amount) independently of whether target.call succeeds.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: paymentOperator is an attacker-controlled or compromised address passed in by the caller.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. execute(target, paymentOperator=AttackerControlled, payload, token=ERC20, amount=X, refund, extraNative=0). 2. transferFrom pulls X to UTBExecutor. 3. approve(AttackerControlled, X). 4. AttackerControlled calls token.transferFrom(UTBExecutor, attacker, X), draining all tokens. 5. remainingBalance ~0; refund skipped. User loses X.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: User / initiator loses ERC20 tokens equal to amount.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: approve never reset; paymentOperator caller-supplied with no validation. HIGH severity fund-loss path; different actor/state from the native refund mechanism.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: approve(paymentOperator, amount) is never reset to zero after the target call regardless of consumption. Residual allowance persists for cross-transaction exploitation.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: paymentOperator who did not consume full allowance can drain the residual in a subsequent call.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. execute() with amount=X, paymentOperator=P. 2. target.call consumes Y<X via P's approval. 3. execute() transfers X-Y back to refund. 4. approve(P,X) still set; P retains allowance; P drains residual when UTBExecutor next holds tokens.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Source: approve never reset. Persistent allowance state distinct from call-time drain; NEEDS_HARNESS for exact cross-tx window.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: remainingBalance underflow / lock if fee-on-transfer or rebasing token causes balanceOf < initBalance
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: `uint remainingBalance = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)) - initBalance;` reverts under 0.8 on underflow, permanently locking tokens (no recovery on revert).
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether protocol supports fee-on-transfer tokens — not visible in source.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: User loses ERC20 stuck in UTBExecutor on revert.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: residual ERC20 allowance exploitation across transactions
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether UTBExecutor retains a token balance between txs enabling residual-allowance drain; sub-transaction timing window.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Future users transiting UTBExecutor if paymentOperator front-runs.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: access-control bypass — permissionless entry into execute()
rejected_mechanisms.claimed_locus: onlyOwner modifier on both execute overloads
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: Both overloads decorated with onlyOwner (Solmate Owned). Only the owner (UTB) can call execute().
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Modifier present/enforced; no permissionless entry to execute itself.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: ERC20 transferFrom reverts causing DoS with no native refund
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: If transferFrom reverts the whole execute reverts; no ETH consumed in that branch before transferFrom; no funds lost.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Revert unwinds all state; retry possible.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: ERC20 tokens drained via paymentOperator approval; native ETH locked not stolen.
impact_direction.victim_loses: End-user loses native ETH permanently stuck when refund reverts; loses ERC20 drained by malicious paymentOperator.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain value correctness: value sent for execution can be permanently lost without delivery or refund.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Mechanism 1 needs only a non-payable refund address; mechanism 2 needs attacker-controlled paymentOperator (caller-supplied, unvalidated). Impact full tx value, not dust, not admin-only.
